text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The price of electricity is to go up from May 1. The oil shale and power pricing commission recommends 60 cents per kwh.
- Right-wing parties have submitted a draft law changing the principles of calculation of the MPs and higher state officials wages and reducing the compensation paid upon resigning.
- The president opened the Estonian embassy in Tokyo.
- Daniel Vaarik, economy ministry PR official, will become the new government spokesman.
- Prime Minister Mart Siimann described the improvement of relations with Russia as one of the priorities of the government.
- An illegal meat-packing factory is selling meat preserves which present a health hazard.
- The parliament legal commission will discuss in a few weeks the abolition of capital punishment.
- Director of the Police Department Ain Seppik received a state decoration on the anniversary of the republic although the interior minister had earlier retracted the application for his decoration.
- Siimann explained his plans for repayment of the one million kroon bank loan he made for the purchase and repair of his apartment.
- An increasing number of Estonian enterprises are expressing interest in selling their shares on the Tallinn stock exchange.
- Banks are selling real estate firms they founded some years ago hoping to earn large profits.
- The Japanese government has offered Estonia an opportunity to study the Japanese markets.
